body: Customer reports they cannot log in since this morning. They reset their password twice and the reset email arrives, but the new password is rejected with "invalid credentials". They use single sign-on through their company's identity provider. Other users at the same company can log in. The customer is on the Business plan and has a board demo at 3pm. They tried two browsers and cleared cookies. Their account shows a recent change of primary email address, made yesterday by their administrator.

The customer was charged twice for the October invoice. Both charges appear on their card statement on the same day for the same amount, 240 euros. Our billing page shows only one paid invoice. They want the duplicate refunded and a corrected receipt for their accountant. They mention this also happened in July and was refunded after a week. They ask whether automatic retries on failed payments could be the cause, since their card was declined once before the second attempt went through.

Exporting a report to CSV produces a file with garbled characters in every name containing accents or umlauts. The customer opens the file in Excel on Windows. The same report exported to PDF looks correct. They have 4,000 contacts with names in German and French and need a clean export for a migration this week. Opening the CSV in a text editor shows the characters correctly, so they suspect an encoding problem rather than corrupted data.

Since the release on Tuesday, calls to the orders endpoint return HTTP 429 after about 50 requests per minute, although the documentation states a limit of 300 per minute for their plan. Their nightly sync job now fails halfway and retries until morning. They have not changed their integration. Response headers show a remaining quota of zero after the fiftieth call. They ask whether the limit changed, and whether it is applied per API key or per account, since they use three keys.

An administrator deleted a shared project by mistake while cleaning up old workspaces. The project contained six months of design files and comments from twelve people. They noticed within an hour. They want to know if the project can be restored, whether comments and version history come back too, and how to stop non-owners from deleting shared projects in future. They are on the Enterprise plan and mention that the audit log shows the deletion at 10:42.

The mobile app crashes immediately on launch for one user after updating to version 5.2 on an older Android phone. Reinstalling did not help. Other people in their team on newer phones are fine. The user relies on the app to scan receipts while travelling and is abroad for two weeks. They ask whether they can download the previous version, and whether their unsynced receipts from the last two days are lost if they clear the app's data.
